summary: Iteration 12 verification of payload field coverage + KB adaptation + review-logs + no-code-fragments requirements for the ACME 'Suspicious PowerShell Encoded Command Execution' offense (5dd6f7e7). All 3 backend pytest cases pass (test_iteration_12.py, 46.6s). Frontend UI on /offenses/5dd6f7e7 → mssp report tab renders the expected report end-to-end: Local LLM badge + Verdict TP badge in header; payload fields grid shows Process=powershell.exe, Parent Process=outlook.exe, Command Line='powershell -nop -w hidden -enc SQBFAFgAKABOAGUA...'; Log source='Sysmon @ 10.10.34.12' (not Custom Rule Engine); Analysis has 3 technical bullets clearly adapted from the KB (mentions Base64/-enc/EncodedCommand/obfuscated); Impact bullet is on-topic; Recommendations list is KB-adapted with 'Review the Sysmon logs and correlate ...' pointer as final bullet; Verdict TP with reason shown at bottom. Section order Analysis → Impact → Recommendations → Verdict is correct. Recommendations text scanned with regex (^\s*\$)|(::)|FromBase64|System\.[A-Z]|powershell\s+-\w|-enc\s → NO code fragments matched. KB entries confirmed present via /api/kb.

minor.issue: Recommendation bullet index 5 leaks the bare LLM section marker 'VARIABLES:' (a raw section header from the model output). _sanitize_bullets in llm_engine.py should drop bullets that are just an all-caps label followed by ':' with no content.

For this offense threat_intel/ioc_enrichment is null (no external IP in payload) yet verdict_reason still says 'Threat Intelligence confirmed 1 malicious indicator(s) linked to this offense.' — misleading wording when there is no ioc_enrichment payload.
Exec summary claims '1 external IP(s) (45.155.204.199)' but offense.external_ips=None and events have no source/destination_ip — inconsistent narrative vs stored fields.

rca of the issue: LLM raw output for this KB-adapted PowerShell offense includes a section header line 'VARIABLES:' between the numbered recommendation bullets and the appended 'Review the Sysmon logs...' pointer. The current _sanitize_bullets in llm_engine.py preserves it because it passes basic length checks and isn't caught by the code-fragment regex (no $, ::, System., -enc). Fix: add a rule to drop bullets matching `^\s*[A-Z][A-Z0-9 _]{1,}:\s*$` (bare section marker) inside _sanitize_bullets, and re-invoke it after _ensure_review_logs to keep ordering clean.
